blocks.content: Article 32 is the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it.

rows: Enforceable for Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights
Applicable throughout the entire territory of India
Limited to the state or territory within its jurisdiction
Discretionary remedy, not a Fundamental Right

items: The writ jurisdiction under Article 226 (High Courts) is broader than under Article 32 (Supreme Court) because High Courts can issue writs for legal rights in addition to Fundamental Rights.
Article 21A (Right to Education) was added to the Constitution via the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
Financial Emergency under Article 360 has never been invoked in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 14 guarantees Equality before Law and Equal Protection of Laws within the territory of India.
Article 21 guarantees Protection of Life and Personal Liberty and has been widely expanded by judicial interpretations.
Article 32 grants the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing individuals to approach the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
Article 356 allows for the imposition of President's Rule in a state upon failure of its constitutional machinery.
Article 368 outlines the procedural powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution.
